did: Built the record a conversation essay moves through, from the topic and the owner's spoken points, through the agent's podcast versions and the owner's flags on them, to the version the owner green-lights. It is an append-only log replayed by a pure state machine, so every version, flag and withdrawal is kept. The next version answers every open flag, says how, and names every turn it changed. A version has any number of speakers, each a cast member with a voice, so an essay is the two-speaker case and a short drama's script is the same record. The owner's choice that they review the podcast and the signature but still edit nothing is recorded as C1536, which moves C1028.

calls.title: Where a conversation's record lives
options: On home as an append-only log, with the mailbox carrying only text between home and the agent
In the repository, beside the calls
calls.why: The topic, flags and notes are the owner's own words, so they belong on home; the agent reaches home through the mailbox, as Rust essays and transcripts already do, and the takes' audio never leaves home (C1535).
calls.undo: Record a call that moves C1535; only the transport changes, not the schema.

calls.title: The record's shape
options: Speakers as cast members with a voice, segues as agent turns, every open flag answered and every change named, a flag may be kept with a reason, the green light closes the record
Owner and agent fixed as the two speakers, a segue as a field on each turn
Flags may stay open across versions, and changes need not be named
calls.why: It keeps owner and agent as roles so a drama fits the same record, and makes every change between versions say which flag it answers (C1537).
calls.undo: Edit ANSWERS_OF, FLAG_VOICE or CONVERSATION_ACCEPTS in packages/video-render/src/conversation.ts behind a /2 schema.

left: HOST12: a too-quiet, too-fast or too-slow flag is answered as conditioned, with the same take in the same turn; the version doesn't yet carry the conditioning's parameters, so adding them to an owner's turn is a /2 schema. ownerTakes(version) lists the takes in order.
HOST13: render a PodcastVersion's turns in order; each turn names its speaker, whose character and voice the version declares.

HOST14: Studio writes the owner's events (topic, point, flag, withdraw, green-light) and reads openFlags and the phase; its words need their own table, since refusalLine is for routines and tests, not a screen.

HOST15: the agent writes version events; a version must answer every open flag exactly once, name every turn it changed by a rewrite or a retake, and a refusal says exactly what it missed. A new point reaches a version only through a flag, such as misses-point with a note.
Home's store for the record and its mailbox folder are not built; C1535 says the shape, and the server and mailbox work falls to HOST14 and HOST15.

For CONVO-GH: turn ids and speaker ids last across versions; a turn keeps its voice; each cast member is at most one speaker per version; recasting a speaker counts as a change to its turns; events must be in date order.
